home.metaDescription: Verify an identity in real time: document, biometrics and a decision, via API or hosted link. Free sandbox.
home.title: Verify identities. Reduce fraud. Stay compliant.
home.lead: A SaaS platform for fast, secure identity checks, document validation and KYC/AML — simple for the user, complete for the business.

hero.verdictSummary: Three checks that agree, and the reasons kept with the case.

vendors.title: The processing we subcontract, named
vendors.note: Others put their customer logos here. We put the list of what we do not do ourselves — it is more useful, and you can check it against our data processing agreement.

home.metricsTitle: Four numbers we can stand behind
home.metricsLead: You will not read an accuracy rate on this page. A rate is measured on volume we have not processed yet, and quoting one before that would be an invention. Here are product properties instead — fixed, and checkable.

metrics.title: Call to get started
metrics.body: One POST creates the verification and returns the link to pass on. There is no mandatory second call before the decision.

metrics.title: Languages served
metrics.body: French and English, in the flow as on this site. The flow follows your customer’s browser language.

metrics.title: Cost of the sandbox
metrics.body: The sandbox answers from fixed data sets, with no billed processing call. No card required at signup.

metrics.title: Media in notifications
metrics.body: No image and no attachment in a notification or an API response. Short-lived signed links only.

home.benefitsTitle: Four reasons to verify rather than take someone’s word

benefits.title: Fewer drop-offs at the door
benefits.body: Quality checks run during capture. An unusable photo is retaken on the spot, not rejected ten minutes later by email.

benefits.title: Something to show later
benefits.body: The timestamped consent, the version of the text accepted, the signals and the decision are kept together. That is what a regulator asks for.

benefits.title: The holder, not just the document
benefits.body: A genuine document in someone else’s hands does not pass: the face is compared to the document, and real presence is checked.

benefits.title: An integration, not a project
benefits.body: One POST, one GET, a sandbox key from signup. Switching to live does not change your code, only the key prefix.

home.stepsTitle: Three steps, one integration to write
home.stepsLead: You create, your customer captures, you decide what happens next. The rest — framing, retries, languages — is our job.

create.title: You create a verification
create.body: One API call, or one click in the console. You get back a time-limited link, to pass on through whichever channel you want.

capture.title: Your customer follows the link
capture.body: Consent, a photo of the document, then a selfie, from their phone. Quality checks run during capture: an unusable photo is retaken on the spot rather than rejected ten minutes later.
capture.deviceLabel: The consent screen of the flow, as your customer sees it on their phone
capture.mockBody: We will ask for a photo of your identity document, then a selfie. Your images are used for this verification only.

decide.title: You receive the decision
decide.body: Processing is asynchronous: poll the verification, or wait for the notification sent to your endpoint. Expect a few minutes.
decide.verdictSummary: Terminal status, reasons kept, and no media in the notification.

home.productLead: No black box announced as one. Every check has a name, a state and a code, and turns up unchanged in the API response.

capabilities.title: Reading the document
capabilities.body: Identity fields are extracted from the photographed document. Where a machine-readable band is present, its own check digits are verified, and any mismatch with the read fields becomes a signal.

capabilities.title: Validity
capabilities.body: An expired document is rejected, with the reason. A deterministic check, not an estimate.

capabilities.title: Face comparison
capabilities.body: The selfie is compared with the photo on the document. The score is not handed over as such: it feeds the decision, and the decision is what you receive.

capabilities.title: Real presence
capabilities.body: A presence check rules out a photo of a screen and a printed portrait held up to the camera.

capabilities.title: Decision rules
capabilities.body: Thresholds and the order they apply in are versioned server-side. Two identical cases return the same decision.

home.decisionTitle: Three outcomes, never a bare score
home.decisionLead: A score on its own defends you neither in front of an unhappy customer nor in front of a regulator. You receive an outcome you can act on, and the reasons that produced it.

outcomes.approvedBody: Supported document, still valid, consistent readings, matching face, presence confirmed.
outcomes.reviewBody: A borderline comparison, a partial machine-readable band. Your team decides from the console, with the extracts and the signals in front of them.
outcomes.rejectedBody: Document outside the corridor, expired document, a different face, or the retry limit reached.
outcomes.note: Reasons are English codes with no personal data: they can be logged and shown to your support team without special handling. The list is documented and versioned with the API — we will not present it as frozen until it is.

home.architectureTitle: Three surfaces, one source of truth
home.architectureLead: You plug in what you need. The hosted link without writing an interface, the API if you drive everything, the console for your team — all three read the same verification.

cards.title: Two calls are enough
cards.body: A POST to create the verification, a GET to read the decision. The rest of the surface is optional.

cards.title: One key, a Bearer token
cards.body: The key prefix states the environment. Switching to live changes nothing else in your code.

cards.title: Idempotency by header
cards.body: Replaying a call after a network drop returns the verification already created, not a billed duplicate.

cards.title: A notification on decision
cards.body: A signed endpoint receives the terminal status. No media inside, only identifiers and reasons.

cards.title: A time-limited link
cards.body: You pass it on through whichever channel you want: email, SMS, or a redirect from your own flow.

cards.title: Capture is our job
cards.body: Framing, retries, error messages, browser support. You write no interface at all.

cards.title: Nothing to install
cards.body: Your customer opens the link in their browser. No app, and no account to create with us.

cards.title: French and English
cards.body: The flow follows the browser language. Two languages genuinely served, not a translation promised.

cards.title: Create without writing code
cards.body: A verification starts from the interface. That is the path for a trial, or for a one-off case to handle by hand.

cards.title: Read a decision back
cards.body: The status, the signals and the reasons are on the case, with the extracts that produced them.

cards.title: Isolation per organisation
cards.body: A verification belongs to one organisation. Another organisation gets a not-found page.

cards.title: Media behind temporary access
cards.body: Even from the console, an image goes through a signed link that expires. There is no permanent URL.

home.compareTitle: What we stand behind, and what we do not claim
home.compareLead: A verification vendor that only states its strengths leaves you to discover its limits in production. Here they are before you sign.

held: A reasoned decision, never a bare score: approved, rejected or review, with its reasons.
Decision rules versioned server-side: two identical cases return the same decision.
A timestamped consent, with the version of the text accepted, kept with the case.
No personal data in our logs: technical identifiers, statuses, durations.
A free and deterministic sandbox, replayable in your continuous integration.
limits: We do not train our own models: reading and biometrics are subcontracted, and named above.
The document corridor is short. A document outside it is rejected as unsupported, not guessed at.
The decision is not instant: processing is asynchronous, expect a few minutes.
We display no certification, because we have obtained none to date.
Reason codes are documented but still being stabilised: they are versioned with the API.

home.devResponseLabel: Response — the link to send your customer
home.trustLead: Technical choices you can check. You will find no certification badge on this site, because we have earned none.

trust.title: Isolation per organisation
trust.body: A verification belongs to one organisation. Another organisation gets a not-found page, not an access denial: a denial would confirm that the resource exists.

trust.title: No personal data in the logs
trust.body: Our logs hold technical identifiers, statuses and durations. Never a name, a document number or an image.

trust.title: Media behind temporary access
trust.body: Photos are never served from a permanent URL. Every view, including from our own console, goes through a signed link that expires.

trust.title: Timestamped consent
trust.body: Your customer accepts the processing before the first photo. The version of the accepted text and the date are kept: that is what lets you demonstrate it later.

home.catalogTitle: One product to sell, two to announce
home.catalogLead: We would rather say it than let you assume it: identity verification is the only product billed today.
home.catalogNote: Biometric authentication and AML screening cannot be enabled, are not priced, and are not exposed through the API. No launch date is announced.
home.closingTitle: Your first verification, without talking to a salesperson
home.closingBody: Create an account, collect the sandbox key and run the whole flow. Nothing billed, no card requested.
home.closingNote: A sales contact exists. It is not the way in.
home.closingListTitle: What you have in hand straight away
closingPoints: A sandbox key as soon as your email address is verified
Deterministic results you can replay in your automated tests
No real personal data to handle in order to integrate

idv.metaDescription: Hosted verification flow, face matched against the identity document, reasoned decision within minutes. A tested document corridor and a free sandbox environment.
idv.heroLead: Your customer photographs their identity document and their face. You receive a reasoned decision, and what you need to justify it later.

heroFacts.title: Hosted flow
heroFacts.body: We handle capture, retries and languages. You write no interface at all.

heroFacts.title: A decision within minutes
heroFacts.body: Processing is asynchronous. The status becomes terminal once the decision is returned.

heroFacts.title: A tested corridor
heroFacts.body: A short list of countries and document types, because it matches what is actually read.

idv.problemTitle: Remotely, a typed name proves nothing
idv.problemBody: Three things have to be tied together: a genuine document, a face that is present, and the same person behind both. Any one of the three on its own is not enough.
idv.insufficientTitle: What proves nothing on its own
insufficient: An identity form filled in by hand
A photo of an identity document sent by email
A selfie with no document to compare it against
idv.insufficientNote: Each of these can be borrowed, rephotographed or retouched. It is cross-checking them that makes the proof.
idv.journeyLead: Hosted by us, on their phone, in French or English depending on their browser.
idv.journeyNote: The flow does not carry your organisation’s branding: that is out of scope today, and we do not sell it as an existing option.

consent.title: Consent
consent.body: The processing is explained and accepted before the first photo. A refusal is recorded and closes the verification.
consent.note: The version of the accepted text and the date are kept.

document.title: Capturing the document
document.body: Guided framing, with sharpness and legibility checked immediately. An unusable photo is retaken on the spot rather than rejected later.
document.docLabel: Illustration: a schematic identity document, with its photo area, its fields and its machine-readable band. No real document, no face.

face.title: Capturing the face
face.body: A selfie, with a presence check to rule out a photo of a screen and a printed portrait held up to the camera.
face.note: No face is enrolled for later reuse: that would be the biometric authentication product, which does not exist yet.

analysis.title: Analysis
analysis.body: Fields are read, consistency checks run, the face is compared, and then the decision rules are applied.
analysis.signalFields: Identity fields read from the document
analysis.signalFace: Face matches the photo on the document

idv.decisionLead: Four possible continuations, one of which is not a decision at all: the retake.
idv.decisionAside: The grey area is not a flaw in the product. It is the case where only your team can decide.
idv.decisionNote: Reasons are stored with the case, as stable English codes and with no personal data.

decisions.approved: The document is supported, readable and still valid, and the face matches the one on the document.
decisions.rejected: A blocking check failed: consent refused, document outside the corridor, expired document, a different face, or the retry limit reached. The reason comes with the decision.
decisions.review: The result is ambiguous — a borderline comparison, a partial machine-readable band. Your analyst decides from the console.
decisions.recapture: This is not a decision, it is a request: the photo is unusable or one side is missing, and the flow hands control back to your customer.

idv.corridorLead: The list is short because it is tested. It will grow when a corridor has genuinely been validated, and not before.
idv.corridorNote: A document outside this list is rejected, with the matching reason. You will find no “and the rest of the world” under this table, and no count of supported documents.
idv.integrationTitle: Two routes, only one to write
idv.integrationLead: The hosted link is enough for most integrations. The API is there to drive and to read.

integration.hostedBody: You create the verification and send the link you get back. The flow, the retries, the languages and the quality checks are our job. It is the fastest route, and the one we recommend.
integration.apiBody: You read statuses and decisions from your own back office, and trigger your own processing when the notification arrives.

idv.sandboxTitle: Write your integration before you have a customer
idv.sandboxBody: Every account starts with a sandbox key. The sandbox returns deterministic results: you replay your cases — approved, rejected, review — without debiting credit and with no real data.
sandbox: A sandbox key as soon as the account is created
Reproducible cases for your automated tests
No real personal data to handle in order to integrate
Going live changes nothing but the key

biometric.metaDescription: Re-authenticate an already verified customer by their face. A product announced on the Recogniz-Me roadmap: it is not available and is not sold.
biometric.noticeBody: It cannot be purchased, enabled, or called through the API. This page exists so you know where the product is going, not to sell it to you today.
biometric.problemTitle: Recognising someone you have already verified
biometric.problemBody: Once a person has been verified, asking for their identity document again at every sensitive operation is expensive — for them as much as for you.
biometric.problemDetail: Recognising their face would be enough to restore trust in seconds: signing in from a new device, before a transfer, or after a password reset. This is the product we want to build next.
biometric.plannedLead: They are listed as “not yet built”, because none of them is implemented. No API code exists for them yet, and we will not invent one to make the page look finished.
planned: Attach a reference face to an already verified identity
Confirm a known person before a sensitive operation
Tell a person who is present from a photo held up to the camera
Return a reasoned confirmation, in the same shape as identity verification
notYet: No performance commitment would be honest at this stage
biometric.ctaBody: Tell us about your use case. We notify the people who asked when the product opens, and their constraints shape the order of the work.
biometric.availableInstead: In the meantime, identity verification is the product that is available, and it covers onboarding.

aml.metaDescription: Sanctions, politically exposed persons and adverse media screening. A product announced on the Recogniz-Me roadmap: it is not available and is not sold.
aml.noticeBody: It cannot be purchased, enabled, or called through the API. This page exists so you know where the product is going, not to sell it to you today.
aml.problemTitle: Knowing whether you are allowed to onboard someone
aml.problemBody: Checking that an identity is real does not tell you whether regulation allows you to open an account for that person.
aml.problemDetail: Screening answers that second question, by checking an already verified identity against sanctions lists, registers of politically exposed persons and the press. It is a compliance product, not a fraud detection product.
aml.plannedLead: They are listed as “not yet built”. The data sources are not settled, so nothing is implemented and nothing is promised.
planned: Check a verified identity against international sanctions lists
Flag a politically exposed person, or a close associate
Surface adverse media attached to the person
Keep a record of every screening for your compliance file
notYet: No list coverage is announced, since the sources are not settled
aml.ctaBody: Tell us which obligations apply to you. They are what will decide the shape of this product, and where it sits in our priorities.
aml.availableInstead: In the meantime, identity verification is available: it is what produces the verified identity a screening will later plug into.

security.metaDescription: Isolation per organisation, encryption, no personal data in the logs, retention periods. What Recogniz-Me puts in place, and what it does not claim to have.
security.title: What we do with the data you trust us with
security.lead: An identity document and a face are among the most sensitive data a platform can handle. This page describes our technical choices, without the vocabulary of certification.

pillars.title: Isolation
pillars.body: One organisation sees nothing of another. A resource belonging to someone else answers like a resource that does not exist.

pillars.title: Logs without identity
pillars.body: Technical identifiers, statuses, durations. No name, no document number, no image.

pillars.title: Temporary media
pillars.body: No permanent URL. Every view goes through a signed link that expires.

security.measuresTitle: The choices that hold the service up
security.measuresLead: Five points, described for what they do. The matching contractual commitments live in the data processing agreement.
security.isolationBody: Every verification belongs to one organisation. Every read is filtered by the organisation of the key that asked. A resource belonging to another customer returns a not-found page rather than an access denial: a denial would confirm that the resource exists.
security.keysBody: Keys are stored as a digest: we cannot read them back. A key’s secret is shown once, when it is created. Test keys and live keys are distinct, and a live key is refused if the balance is insufficient.
security.mediaBody: Media are stored in private storage. No permanent URL is published: every view, including from our own console, goes through a short-lived signed link. Binary content never travels in our business responses or in our notifications.
security.transitBody: Traffic runs over HTTPS. Media and the database are encrypted at rest by the underlying storage. Flow links are short-lived tokens, invalidated after use.
security.consentBody: The flow collects the person’s explicit consent before any capture, in their own language. The version of the accepted text, the date and a fingerprint of the IP address are kept: that is what makes it possible to demonstrate later that consent was indeed collected.
security.logsTitle: What we write down, and what we do not
security.logsBody: Our logs exist to run the service, not to keep identities. They hold technical identifiers, statuses and durations. The rule applies to our error traces too: an incident is diagnosed with a request identifier, not with someone’s name.
logsNeverItems: Name, date of birth, document number
An image of a document or of a face
A password, an API key secret, a hosted link token
A card number — we store none
security.retentionLead: Images and the decision do not share the same fate: that is what lets you keep what serves your compliance without keeping the photos.

retentionRows.duration: Deleted on request; otherwise kept as long as the decision has to be justified
A short period, with no personal data

security.retentionNote: You can ask for the media of a verification to be deleted. The decision and its audit trail are kept separately: that is what remains useful to your compliance without holding on to the images.
security.claimsBody: This page is not a substitute for an audit. We would rather write that down than leave you to guess.
claims: We hold neither SOC 2, nor ISO 27001, nor any presence-detection certification.
We do not announce compliance that an auditor has not observed.
We do not display a subprocessor’s certification badge as though it were ours.
security.contactBody: Write to us. We answer, we fix, and we do not pursue anyone who told us in good faith.

docs.heroNote: The examples work as they are with a sandbox key.
docs.responseLabel: Response — the link to send your customer
docs.authBody: Every request carries your key as a Bearer token. A key starting with ky_test_ works in the sandbox, a ky_live_ key on real data. That is the only difference between your two environments.
authPoints: A key’s secret is shown once, when it is created.

docs.step2Body: The response holds the verification identifier and the link to send your customer. The idempotency header protects your network retries: replaying the same call does not create a duplicate.
docs.step3Body: Poll the verification, or wait for the notification we will send to your endpoint. The status is terminal once it reads approved, rejected, expired or cancelled.
docs.endpointsLead: Four calls in the current scope. Media uploads go through signed URLs and the flow’s own routes, never through your key.

terms.metaDescription: Terms of service for the Recogniz-Me identity verification service. A draft under legal review.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.body: Recogniz-Me provides an identity verification service accessible through a programming interface and through a web console. These terms govern the use of that service by a customer organisation and by the people it authorises.

sections.heading: Account and organisation
sections.body: Access requires a named account attached to an organisation. The customer is responsible for the access it grants, for the confidentiality of the API keys issued to its organisation, and for the use made under those keys.

sections.heading: Expected use
sections.body: The service is used to verify the identity of people who have been informed of it and have consented to it. It is not used to monitor a person without their knowledge, nor to build a biometric database detached from a verification purpose.

sections.heading: Environments
sections.body: The sandbox returns simulated results and must not receive real personal data. The live environment requires a sufficient credit balance; a live key is refused otherwise.

sections.heading: Nature of the decision
sections.body: The service returns a reasoned decision based on the elements provided. That decision is one input among others: the responsibility for onboarding a person, or not, belongs to the customer. No result is guaranteed to be correct in every case.

sections.heading: Availability
sections.body: The service is provided without a contractual service level commitment at this stage. Planned interruptions are announced where they can be foreseen.

sections.heading: Billing
sections.body: Live verifications are counted when they are created and debited from organisation credit. Sandbox never debits. MVP top-up is by card. Without a sufficient balance, live keys are refused.

sections.heading: Personal data
sections.body: The customer is the controller, Recogniz-Me acts as processor. Roles, commitments and further subprocessors are described in the data processing agreement.

sections.heading: Termination for breach
sections.body: Use that runs counter to these terms, in particular use without the consent of the people concerned, may lead to immediate suspension of access.

sections.heading: Changes to these terms
sections.body: Any substantial change is notified before it takes effect, with a reasonable period in which to cancel free of charge.

privacy.metaDescription: Data processed by Recogniz-Me, purposes, retention periods and the rights of individuals. A draft under legal review.

sections.heading: Two situations to keep apart
sections.body: This policy covers two distinct kinds of processing. First, the data of this site’s visitors and of our console’s users, for which Recogniz-Me is the controller. Second, the data of verified individuals, which we process on behalf of our customers as a processor: in that case the purpose and the legal basis are set by the customer who asked for the verification.

sections.heading: This site
sections.body: This site is static and sets no analytics or advertising cookie. No third-party tracker is loaded, and the fonts are served from our own domain. The language is inferred from the preferences your browser sends.

sections.heading: Contact form
sections.body: The information you enter is used to answer your message. It is not resold, nor used for outreach unrelated to your request.

sections.heading: Console users
sections.body: We process an email address, a name, a password as a digest, and a record of sensitive actions. These serve to open access, to secure the account and to answer a complaint.

sections.heading: Verified individuals
sections.body: For a verification, we process the images of the identity document and of the face, the identity fields read from the document, the technical signals of the check, and the record of consent. These serve solely to return the decision our customer asked for.

sections.heading: Biometric data
sections.body: Comparing the face with the photo on the document is processing of biometric data. It rests on the explicit consent collected at the start of the flow, whose date and text version are kept.

sections.heading: What we do not keep
sections.body: Our technical logs contain no personal data: no name, no document number, no image. We store no card number; payment is handled by our payment provider.

sections.heading: Retention periods
sections.body: Flow links expire within an hour. Images are deleted at the request of the responsible customer; failing that, they are kept as long as the decision has to be justifiable. The decision, its reasons and the audit trail are kept for the customer’s compliance needs.

sections.heading: Subprocessors
sections.body: We rely on hosting, storage, document analysis and face comparison providers, as well as a payment provider. The named list and the locations appear in the data processing agreement.

sections.heading: Your rights
sections.body: You may ask for access to, correction of, erasure of or restriction of the processing concerning you. If your verification was requested by a company, approach that company first: it decides the purpose. We relay and carry out its decision, and we answer you directly if it does not.

dpa.metaDescription: Outline of the data processing agreement between Recogniz-Me and its customers. A draft under legal review; a signed version is available on request.

sections.heading: Roles
sections.body: The customer is the controller: it determines who is to be verified and for what purpose. Recogniz-Me is the processor and acts only on the customer’s instructions, within the limits of the subscribed service.

sections.heading: Subject matter and duration
sections.body: The purpose of the processing is the identity verification of the people designated by the customer. It lasts for the duration of the contractual relationship, extended by the retention periods needed to justify the decisions returned.

sections.heading: Categories of data and of people
sections.body: The identity data and biometric data of the people the customer submits for verification are processed, as well as the account data of the users of the customer’s console.

sections.heading: Instructions and limits
sections.body: Recogniz-Me does not use the customer’s data for purposes other than providing the service. It is neither resold nor used to train a model without a separate and specific written agreement.

sections.heading: Security measures
sections.body: Isolation per organisation, encryption in transit and at rest, media access through short-lived signed links, logs free of personal data, least privilege on internal access. The detail is on the security page.

sections.heading: Further subprocessors
sections.body: Using further subprocessors is permitted subject to equivalent commitments. The named list is communicated, and any addition is notified with a period allowing objection.

sections.heading: Transfers
sections.body: Processing locations are documented. Any transfer outside the European Economic Area relies on a recognised transfer mechanism.

sections.heading: Assistance to the controller
sections.body: Recogniz-Me assists the customer in answering requests to exercise rights and in its impact assessments, and notifies any data breach it becomes aware of without undue delay.

sections.heading: Fate of the data
sections.body: At the end of the contract, data is deleted or returned at the customer’s choice, subject to any legal retention obligations that would bind either party.

sections.heading: Audit
sections.body: The customer may request the documentary evidence attesting to compliance with these commitments. An on-site audit is arranged at shared cost and without disrupting service for other customers.

dpa.requestBody: This outline is there to prepare your internal review. Ask us for the version to sign, adapted to your scope.
